question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+12y=10 \\ 6x-7y=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

 
According to Cramer's rule, the unknown $y$ can be written as 
$y=\frac{{D}_{y}}{|\begin{aligned}5 & 12 \\ 6 & -7\end{aligned}|}$, where ${D}_{y}=$
question.worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x+12y=10 \\ 6x-7y=-14.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 12 \\ 6 & -7\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to construct ${D}_{y}$, we replace the second column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 10 \\ 6 & -14\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$
